newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. renews observer mission in Georgia for 6 months.
newsitem.headline: U.N. renews observer mission in Georgia for 6 months.

text.p: The Security Council unanimously approved Thursday a six-month rernewal, until January 31, 1998, of the 116-member U.N. Observer Mission in Georgia (UNOMIG), whose Abkhazia region is under the control of separatists.

A 1,500-strong Russian-led peacekeeping force deployed by the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) patrols a buffer zone between Georgia and the breakaway region, from which Georgian troops were driven in 1993 along with hundreds of thousands of refugees.

The CIS force's mandate expires at the end of July, sparking fears of a resumption of the conflict that killed 10,000 people. But Russian military officials said a pullout of the force was not imminent.
The renewal of the small U.N. observer mission is subject to review by the Security Council if any changes are made in the mandate or presence of the CIS force.
The council resolution expressed deep concern at the continued deadlock in achieving a settlement of the Abkhazia conflict.

It reaffirmed the council's commitment to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Georgia within its internationally recognised borders and underlined the unacceptability of any action by the Abkhaz leadership that contravened this.

The council also condemned killings and other ethnically motivated acts of violence amd reaffirmed the right of refugees and displaced persons to return to their homes in secure conditions. It repeated previous demands for the Abkhaz side to accelerate the process of voluntary return of refugees without delay or preconditions.
The resolution condemned the continued laying of mines in the Gali region, on the Abkhaz side of the security zone.

It welcomed efforts by Secretary-General Kofi Annan and his special representative for Georgia, Liviu Bota, to achieve a comprehensive political settlement, as well as efforts by Russia in its capacity of "facilitator."
Annan was asked to submit a new report on the situation in Abkhazia in three months' time.
